questions.question_text: A gardener measures the circumference of a circular pond as $96$ cm and divides by $3$ to estimate the diameter. Compared with the true diameter, her estimate is:

options.text: too large, because $3$ is smaller than $\pi$
too small, because $3$ is smaller than $\pi$
options.why: Compares $3$ with $\pi$ correctly but reverses the effect: dividing by a smaller number gives a larger result.
Treats $\pi$ as exactly $3$ rather than $3.14159\ldots$, so no error is expected at all.

options.text: too small, because $3$ is larger than $\pi$
options.why: States the comparison the wrong way round; $3$ is smaller than $\pi$, not larger.

questions.solution_text:
Estimate: $\frac{96}{3} = 32\text{ cm}$
True diameter: $\frac{96}{\pi} = 30.56\text{ cm}$
The estimate is too large, because dividing by $3$ instead of the larger $\pi$ gives a larger result.
